extracted.intended_audience: poets, translators, and writers submitting poems or letters to Poetry magazine (Poetry Foundation)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting poetry (and visual poetry) and letters to Poetry magazine: what the magazine accepts, file formats, submission limits, rights and payment, timelines, and procedural instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall selection standard
rubrics_metrics.description: We examine all work received and accept that which seems best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The magazine considers all submissions and selects work judged to be the best. This is a general quality standard; no further scoring rubric is provided. The page also notes they consider original works in English and translations into English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible language and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: We consider original works written in the English language as well as translations of poetry into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both original English-language poems and translations into English are eligible for submission. No additional detail on translation credits or formatting beyond standard submission rules is provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: No previously published material
rubrics_metrics.description: No. We cannot consider anything that has been previously published or accepted for publication, anywhere, in any form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that has appeared online is considered to have been previously published and should not be submitted. This prohibition covers any prior publication or acceptance in any form or venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment and rights for published work
rubrics_metrics.description: Payment is made on publication at the rate of $10 per line (with a minimum payment of $300), and $150 per page of prose, for first serial rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment applies on publication; payment rates: $10/line (minimum $300) for poetry, $150 per page of prose. Payment is for first serial rights. All rights will revert to the author upon publication. Authors receive two contributor copies of the issue in which their work appears.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method (no paper submissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of July 2013, we no longer accept paper submissions. We now have an online system for you to send us your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit via the online submission manager at poetry.submittable.com. The system securely sends editors your work and emails a confirmation of receipt. Your Submittable account will be set up during your first submission; there is no need to create an account beforehand. If having trouble, contact Submittable support (support@submittable.com or 855.467.8264).

rubrics_metrics.name: Status checks via Submittable
rubrics_metrics.description: Once you have submitted your work, you can check the status of your submission by signing into your Submittable account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission tracking and status updates are managed through the Submittable account created during submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed file types (Poetry category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the 'Poetry' category, submit files in one of the following formats only: Word document (.doc) files, Rich Text Format (.rtf) files, Text (.txt) files, Portable Document Format (.pdf) files, Word Perfect (.ppf) files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Files must be submitted in one of the specified formats when using the Poetry category. Non-listed file types may not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed file types (Visual Poetry category)
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual Poetry category accepts the following: JPEG, TIFF, PNG, PDF, and Word document files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual/graphic work should be submitted in one of these image or document formats under the Visual Poetry category.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission quantity and file formatting limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that submissions are limited to four poems (1 file), and should not exceed ten pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit poems in a single file with poems separated by titles or page breaks. Include all writer contact information on the first page of the submitted file. Adhering to these limits helps ensure timely reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-submission policy / do not send multiple submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions year round. We ask that you do not make multiple submissions: please wait for a response to your submission before sending new work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waiting for a response before submitting additional work is requested; multiple simultaneous submissions are discouraged and may delay processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time / patience expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: We will do our best to respond within seven months from the day of receipt, but are sometimes slower in responding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The staff aims for responses within seven months, but delays can occur. The note emphasizes patience and that adhering to submission limits (four poems or fewer) helps ensure a timely response because each submission receives a 'good read.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Email deliverability instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Please ensure that you set your e-mail spam filter to allow mail from both poetryfoundation.org and poetrymagazine.org; otherwise notification regarding your submission may be marked as junk mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters are responsible for ensuring they receive correspondence by whitelisting the magazine's domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support contact for submission issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Who can I contact if I'm having trouble using the online system? Please contact Submittable by e-mail (support@submittable.com) or by phone: 855.467.8264.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical or account problems with Submittable should be directed to Submittable support; general editorial queries are not described here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Familiarity with the magazine before submitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone contemplating a submission is encouraged to examine the magazine before sending a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should read the magazine (subscribe or order a single copy) to understand the publication's editorial style and preferences before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters to the Editor — desired content
rubrics_metrics.description: Poetry is looking for thought-provoking responses to work published in the magazine, as well as letters that raise new questions about the state of contemporary poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should engage with published work or larger questions about contemporary poetry; the emphasis is on thoughtful, question-raising responses rather than simple praise or complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters submission process and timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: To send us your letter, please fill out the form here. If we choose to use your letter, we will notify you by phone. If you have not heard from us within two weeks of sending your letter, you may assume we will not be using it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters are submitted via an online form; selected writers will be contacted by phone. Lack of contact within two weeks indicates non-selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters editing and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: All letters may be edited for length and clarity, and may appear online, in print, or both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should expect editorial edits for brevity and clarity and potential publication in multiple formats; retention of original wording is not guaranteed.
